message.reasoning_content:
The user wants the sum of integers from 1 to 1000 that are divisible by 3 or 5, with duplicates (divisible by both 3 and 5, i.e., divisible by 15) counted only once.

This is the classic inclusion-exclusion problem.

Sum = (sum of multiples of 3) + (sum of multiples of 5) - (sum of multiples of 15)

**Sum of multiples of 3 from 1 to 1000:**
Largest multiple of 3 ≤ 1000: 999 = 3 × 333, so n = 333
Sum = 3 × (1 + 2 + ... + 333) = 3 × 333 × 334 / 2 = 3 × 55611 = 166833

Let me verify: 333 × 334 = 333 × 300 + 333 × 34 = 99900 + 11322 = 111222
111222 / 2 = 55611
55611 × 3 = 166833 ✓

**Sum of multiples of 5 from 1 to 1000:**
Largest multiple of 5 ≤ 1000: 1000 = 5 × 200, so n = 200
Sum = 5 × (1 + 2 + ... + 200) = 5 × 200 × 201 / 2 = 5 × 20100 = 100500

Let me verify: 200 × 201 = 40200
40200 / 2 = 20100
20100 × 5 = 100500 ✓

**Sum of multiples of 15 from 1 to 1000:**
Largest multiple of 15 ≤ 1000: 990 = 15 × 66, so n = 66
Sum = 15 × (1 + 2 + ... + 66) = 15 × 66 × 67 / 2 = 15 × 2211 = 33165

Let me verify: 66 × 67 = 4422
4422 / 2 = 2211
2211 × 15 = 33165 ✓

**Final answer:**
166833 + 100500 - 33165 = 234168

Let me verify: 166833 + 100500 = 267333
267333 - 33165 = 234168

The answer is 234168.

results.answer:
# Smallest Positive Integer Divisible by All Integers from 1 to 20

This is the **Least Common Multiple (LCM)** of the integers 1 through 20.

## Strategy: Prime Factorization

For each number from 1 to 20, I find its prime factorization, then take the **highest power of each prime** that appears.

| Number | Prime Factorization |
|--------|-------------------|
| 1 | — |
| 2 | 2 |
| 3 | 3 |
| 4 | 2² |
| 5 | 5 |
| 6 | 2 · 3 |
| 7 | 7 |
| 8 | **2³** |
| 9 | **3²** |
| 10 | 2 · 5 |
| 11 | 11 |
| 12 | 2² · 3 |
| 13 | 13 |
| 14 | 2 · 7 |
| 15 | 3 · 5 |
| 16 | **2⁴** |
| 17 | 17 |
| 18 | 2 · 3² |
| 19 | 19 |
| 20 | 2² · 5 |

## Selecting the Highest Power of Each Prime

| Prime | Highest power needed | Source |
|-------|---------------------|--------|
| 2 | **2⁴ = 16** | from 16 |
| 3 | **3² = 9** | from 9 (or 18) |
| 5 | **5¹ = 5** | from 5, 10, 15, or 20 |
| 7 | **7¹ = 7** | from 7 or 14 |
| 11 | **11¹ = 11** | from 11 |
| 13 | **13¹ = 13** | from 13 |
| 17 | **17¹ = 17** | from 17 |
| 19 | **19¹ = 19** | from 19 |

## Computing the LCM

$$\text{LCM} = 2^4 \times 3^2 \times 5 \times 7 \times 11 \times 13 \times 17 \times 19$$

Step by step:

$$2^4 \times 3^2 = 16 \times 9 = 144$$
$$144 \times 5 = 720$$
$$720 \times 7 = 5040$$
$$5040 \times 11 = 55440$$
$$55440 \times 13 = 720720$$
$$720720 \times 17 = 12252240$$
$$12252240 \times 19 = 232792560$$

## Answer

$$\boxed{232{,}792{,}560}$$

This is the smallest positive integer divisible by every integer from 1 to 20.
